Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, when constant lookup raises LoadError, ActiveSupport::Inflector#safe_constantize (and String#safe_constantize) builds a regular expression from the requested constant name without escaping it, so a caller that passes untrusted input lets the attacker choose the source of a pattern that the application compiles. Crafted patterns can trigger defects in Ruby's regular expression compiler, possibly leading to a crash of the server process, and repeated requests could keep the application unavailable. Action Cable passes the channel value of each subscribe command to safe_constantize before any channel lookup, so an unauthenticated client can reach this code when the application mounts Action Cable and accepts connections from untrusted clients without an added authentication check. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.

CVE-2026-74583.title: net/sched: cls_route: fix fastmap use-after-free on filter
CVE-2026-74583.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: cls_route: fix fastmap use-after-free on filter

The route4 classifier maintains a 16-slot fastmap cache that stores raw
struct route4_filter pointers indexed by (id, iif). The reader
(route4_classify) populates this cache via route4_set_fastmap() for every
classified packet that hits a filter. The writer (route4_delete,
route4_change) clears the cache via route4_reset_fastmap() before
RCU-deferred kfree of the filter.

This creates a UAF race:
1. Reader walks the RCU-protected bucket chain, finds filter f
2. Writer unlinks f, calls route4_reset_fastmap(), then tcf_queue_work()
3. Reader calls route4_set_fastmap() and writes f into the cache
*after* the writer's reset, caching a pointer about to be freed
4. After the RCU grace period, kfree(f) executes
5. Next classified packet on the same (id, iif) tuple hits the stale
fastmap entry and reads f->res from freed memory

CVE-2026-99245.title: KEYS: Fix key_reject_and_link() race with keyring restriction
CVE-2026-99245.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KEYS: Fix key_reject_and_link() race with keyring restriction

The restrict_link check in key_reject_and_link() is done before taking
the keyring semaphore, racing with a concurrent keyring_restrict()
that installs the restriction while holding the semaphore in write
mode.

Move the check to after __key_link_lock(), so it is done under the
semaphore, matching the pattern used in __key_create_or_update().

CVE-2026-99388.title: smb: smbdirect: fix buffer length underflow in RDMA transfers
CVE-2026-99388.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: fix buffer length underflow in RDMA transfers

When a remote buffer descriptor is larger than the remaining local
buffer, smbdirect_connection_rdma_xmit() clamps its length and sets
buf_len to zero. The common accounting code then subtracts the clamped
length from buf_len, causing it to underflow. If another descriptor
follows, the loop processes it with a wrapped remaining length and
includes memory beyond the local buffer in the RDMA transfer.

A client can trigger an out-of-bounds kernel write with an SMB WRITE
request, or an out-of-bounds kernel read with an SMB READ request, by
supplying multiple RDMA buffer descriptors with an oversized descriptor
before the last one.

Remove the premature assignment to buf_len. Subtracting the clamped length
already consumes the remaining buffer, so the next iteration stops and
only descriptors within the local buffer are used to build work requests.
